payload.headline: Amazon flat at 257.89 near top of value range; cash burn keeps us waiting

summary.thesis: Amazon's margins are improving, but slowing sales growth, heavy cash burn and a price near the top of its own value range leave little room for error.
summary.decision: Long-term: wait for a lower price. Swing: no trade while the price sits just under resistance.

payload.happening: Amazon closed at 257.89, up 0.05%, in the middle of a sideways range, with resistance just above at 261.12–266.4. The Financial Times reported that voter backlash threatens Amazon's $17bn Ohio AI data centre. The other news is small product discounts. No earnings date is in the data, and options to 2026-11-20 price a move of about 4.0%.
payload.business: Three facts change the business. Sales growth is slowing: the latest quarter grew 12.09% from a year earlier, down from 16.61% two quarters ago. Profitability is improving: operating margin (profit from operations per dollar of sales) rose to 13.09% from 11.02%. Cash is going the other way. Free cash flow (cash left after running the business and paying for investment) was -46.9B over the last 12 months, against +10.6B a year earlier. Debt of 180.9B exceeds cash of 55.8B, leaving net debt of 66.7B. The filings flag that unpaid customer bills are up 61% while sales are up 12%, which may mean sales were pulled forward or customers are paying more slowly. They also note that margin is at the top of its 5-year range of 2–13%. The Ohio report is reported, not confirmed by a filing. It puts one large AI build at risk from local politics. It does not touch current demand or margins, but it could delay future AI capacity. Funding is not at risk: liquidity (cash plus available credit) is 114.2B. The discount headlines change nothing.

worth.text: There is no discounted-cash-flow value, because free cash flow is negative. The only valuation method compares the price-to-sales ratio (price divided by sales per share) with Amazon's own last 5 years. That gives 187.93 at the low end, 238.65 in the middle and 265.96 at the high end. At 257.89 the price sits above the middle and close to the top. Amazon's price-to-sales of 3.5 is at the 70th percentile of its own 5-year history. By the same measure it looks cheap next to peers, whose median is 6.7, and its growth-adjusted EV/sales is 0.59 of the peer level. That gap is the main disagreement between the two views. Earnings tell a stretched story: the stock costs 20.1 times this year's expected earnings but 24.2 times next year's, because analysts expect EPS of 10.67 next year, below 12.8 this year. The filings estimate that the price needs about 34% yearly growth, while Amazon has delivered 13% a year over 3 years.
worth.key_assumption: Amazon's price-to-sales stays within its own 5-year range instead of moving toward the peer median of 6.7.

bull: Price-to-sales of 3.5 is about half the peer median of 6.7, and the growth-adjusted ratio is 0.59 of peers.
Operating margin rose to 13.09% from 11.02%, so each dollar of sales now earns more.
Analysts raised next-year EPS estimates by 1.4% over 30 days to 10.67, and liquidity of 114.2B can fund the investment.
bear: Free cash flow fell to -46.9B over 12 months, from +10.6B a year earlier, and net debt is 66.7B.
Quarterly sales growth slowed to 12.09% from 16.61% two quarters ago, while the price needs about 34% a year.
Unpaid customer bills are up 61% against 12% sales growth, and next-year EPS of 10.67 is below this year's 12.8.

levels.what: Top of the nearest support zone (249.71–251.93). No buying above it; a small first entry here only if the next filing shows free cash flow better than -46.9B.
Bottom of the stronger support zone (8 touches), near the 200-day average of 244.76. A close below it breaks the range.
Middle of the own-history value range, where price meets fair value. This is the main buy level.

longterm.why: Better margins do not yet outweigh slower growth and cash burn at a price near the 265.96 top of the value range. The business grade is D and the committee call is 'Reduce'.

swing.why: The price sits in its own zone (255.19–259.49), just below resistance at 261.12. The room to resistance is smaller than one typical day's move (ATR, the average daily range, is 8.91), so the reward does not justify a stop below support at 249.71. With no trend (20-, 50- and 200-day averages all flat), there is no clean setup.

decision.timing: No earnings date is in the data, so the next decision points are price-based: a test of 251.93, or a close above 266.4. Options to 2026-12-18 price a move of about 8.6%.

change_mind: A close above 266.4, the top of resistance and above the 265.96 value ceiling, together with a next filing that shows free cash flow better than -46.9B, would turn this into a hold.
A fall to 238.65 with operating margin holding at or above 13.09% would turn wait into buy.
A close below 244.3 or next-year EPS estimates cut below 10.67 would push the action from wait to avoid.
payload.what_changed: Unchanged: still wait; the price held near 257.89 under resistance at 261.12 while free cash flow stays at -46.9B, though options now price more movement (implied volatility 43.4 vs realized 40.1) than yesterday.
payload.label: Research, not advice.
